user.title: Set up Blink Live View Proxy
user.description: Blink Live View Proxy needs a companion proxy that signs in to Blink. On Home Assistant OS or Supervised, Home Assistant can install it for you as an add-on, after you confirm.

menu_options.connect: Connect to a proxy I already run (add-on, Linux or Docker)

install_companion.title: Install the companion add-on?
install_companion.description:
If you continue, Home Assistant will ask the Supervisor to add the project's add-on repository ({repository}) when it is not already there, and to install the Blink Live View Proxy add-on from it.

Nothing else changes: an add-on you already have is left alone, the add-on is not started, and no Blink account is used. You will set up and start it yourself on the next screen. Close this dialog to make no changes.

install_failed.title: Check companion installation
install_failed.description: Supervisor could not confirm the installation ({reason}). A build may still be running; checking again waits for that build instead of starting another. You can also connect to a proxy you already run.

menu_options.connect: I'll set up the proxy myself

companion_ready.title: Finish setting up the add-on
companion_ready.description:
The companion add-on is installed but still needs you. Open Settings → Apps (Add-ons on older versions), open Blink Live View Proxy, enter your Blink username and password under Configuration, and start it. When its log says Blink sent a PIN, enter that PIN in the blink_2fa_code option and save, without restarting.

Then come back here and continue. The proxy address and token are filled in for you.

connect.title: Blink Live View Proxy
connect.description: Connect Home Assistant to the local Blink live-view proxy. Live-view duration controls how long the direct player asks the proxy to keep each stream open; Blink may still end a session early.

data_description.stream_seconds: Allowed range: 10-300 seconds. Longer sessions can use more Blink live-view quota and may run into camera or cloud-side limits.

reauth_confirm.title: Blink Live View Proxy token
reauth_confirm.description: The proxy rejected the stored token. Enter the current proxy token; if the add-on shared one, it is filled in for you.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the proxy.

abort.reauth_failed: The config entry is no longer available.

progress.install_companion: Installing the companion add-on. Pulling its image can take a few minutes; you can leave this page open.

init.title: Blink Live View Proxy Options
init.description: Update the local proxy connection settings. Live-view duration controls how long the direct player asks the proxy to keep each stream open; Blink may still end a session early.

data_description.stream_seconds: Allowed range: 10-300 seconds. Longer sessions can use more Blink live-view quota and may run into camera or cloud-side limits.
data_description.blink_poll_seconds: How often the proxy refreshes Blink for the camera snapshots, motion, battery, temperature and alarm entities. Allowed range: 60-3600 seconds. A failed refresh backs off and never signs in again.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the proxy.

proxy_outdated.title: The Blink proxy is older than this integration needs
proxy_outdated.description:
The proxy at {base_url} reports {proxy_version}. This integration needs {minimum_version} or newer.

Live view, clips and push-to-talk keep working. What fails is anything the newer proxy added — browser authentication answers 404, because those routes have never existed in that build.

The two halves update independently: Marketplace (HACS on older versions) updates the integration, and nothing moves the proxy. On a Linux service install, run this on the proxy host from a checkout of the repository:

```
sudo scripts/install-proxy.sh
```

It keeps your token, config and Blink session, and restarts the service. Add-on installs update from the add-on store.

This notice clears itself once the proxy reports {minimum_version} or newer.

proxy_outdated_fixable.title: The Blink proxy is older than this integration needs

confirm.title: Update the Blink proxy
confirm.description:
The proxy at {base_url} reports {proxy_version}.

Home Assistant will ask it to run the updater it was installed with, which fetches the newest release and restarts the proxy. Any live view playing at that moment stops, and clips, tokens and your Blink session are kept.

For a systemd proxy, the dialog closes once the updater starts. For an add-on, it waits for Supervisor to finish the update. This notice clears itself within a minute or two after the proxy comes back and reports its new version.

abort.already_running: An update is already running on the proxy. Give it a minute, then check whether this notice has cleared on its own.
abort.not_supported: This proxy cannot update itself. Update it the way it was installed: re-run scripts/install-proxy.sh on the host, or pull the new image and recreate the container.
abort.no_addon: Supervisor does not list a Blink Live View Proxy add-on, so there is nothing here to update. Update it from Settings → Apps (Add-ons on older versions).
abort.entry_gone: This proxy is no longer set up in Home Assistant, so there is nothing left to update.
abort.update_failed: The proxy could not be asked to update. Check that it is reachable and that the token is still valid, then look at the proxy host's logs.
